author: Codex
notes: Author analysis of all pinned source bytes, not independent review or passing coverage. The Windows ten-span mapping and native counterparts require separate review and matching C evidence.

Most IO code is guarded by successful opening of os.tmpname. Date/version output alone can still occur after that block is skipped; acceptance must require the IO section witnesses and reject the temporary-file omission.

Run with _soft and _port unset. Instrumented POSIX execution must have T.nonblock; a false capability guard cannot close partial-write coverage. Windows executes the separately named native pipe counterpart.

The source launches two empty-command Lua children and four typed-exit Lua children via popen and execute. POSIX instrumented adds one bare-lua receiver. The harness adds two configuration probes: totals are eight/nine Ada and four/five normal-return C telemetry records. C os.exit bypasses its CLI writer.
Embedded Lua chunks, generated date assertions and shell receiver assertions are dynamic obligations, not inert strings or lexical pass evidence.

sections.invariant: PATH exists; input/output defaults use real full userdata and FILE* metatable identity; standard streams cannot be closed. Missing/invalid receiver, unsupported io.type values and failing paths return the specified errors and native error triples. Error-helper bodies are invoked throughout the file.

Temporary-file setup cannot skip the IO block. Opening mode validation, locale selection, failing loadfile/dofile, registry-owned defaults, seeks and writes work. Replacing default output permits its old stream to be finalized and restores stdout identity. Windows replaces only its native temporary-path/standard-input-seek assumptions with reviewed counterparts.

Six hundred rounds of default input, temporary file and iterator creation survive repeated collection without leaking handles. Explicit default close, rename/failing rename, append and lexical close work; the escaped closed object retains userdata identity and closed tostring.

Decimal/hexadecimal integers and hexadecimal floats preserve values including integer boundaries and signs. New and starred formats work. Multiple-format reads preserve result order and terminate at the first failed conversion, with exact newline and byte consumption.

The loaded file yields twice through dofile and resumes with two then one values; the final arithmetic return uses both suspended activations' state. This requires iterative execution transfer through the native callback path.

Numeric scanning consumes exactly valid decimal/hex prefixes and leaves punctuation or malformed suffixes for following byte reads. An overlong numeral fails with unread zero suffix retained; repeated invalid scans and EOF zero-byte probes preserve position and result arity.

io.lines owns and closes its file at EOF and rejects later calls; file:lines leaves ownership to the caller. Default-input iterators agree with explicit file iterators, captured handles survive until cleanup, and 250 formats work while a 251st is rejected without leaking the opened file.

Read-only writes produce native error triples. Line, keep-newline, number, fixed-byte, zero-byte and whole-file reads distinguish EOF correctly and return no spurious extra results. Relative/absolute seeking and flush preserve contents; closed registry defaults reject read/write.
Reading a write-only stream, writing a read-only stream and iterating an unreadable stream report textual errors with numeric codes where specified; handles remain explicitly closable.

L retains newline and final unterminated text across all iterator forms; l removes newline. A line iterator feeds load with an explicit environment, and the resulting code performs its expected assignments.

debug.getlocal exposes the third (for state) variable as the fourth closing value. io.lines' handle is open inside the loop and closed after both break and a propagated error, including the handle used as the error object.

Buffered writes to the sink flush successfully. Buffered writes to the failing device initially succeed but explicit file/default flush fails, and close follows the required semantics. Windows uses an actual failing FILE stream counterpart; macOS device availability needs native baseline evidence, not a broad portability skip.

Iterator result tuples terminate correctly on partial EOF, numbers and whole-file reads. load from line-without-newline fails where token boundaries change; line-with-newline, one-byte and three-byte readers execute correctly. Quoted strings and final comments round-trip through loadfile and files are removed.

Empty files, initial comments without newline, BOMs and initial-comment line numbers load correctly. Binary files preserve zero/255 bytes and multiple returns, including no-upvalue functions and prefixed comments. Explicit table/nil/default environments and text/binary mode rejection are distinct.

Two real file userdata retain distinct identity across default-stream changes. Binary reads preserve zero and byte 255 without confusing EOF; mixed fixed/number/line/all reads retain ordering and terminate correctly, with explicit close and removal.

Full buffering hides pending output from a second reader until close; line buffering exposes output after newline. Preserve the exact upstream no-buffer sequence, but do not claim it independently proves a successful unbuffered write: its io.open call omits the write mode and its write result is unchecked. Separate focused native tests must cover that stronger contract.

An unbuffered failing device reports positive errno and zero written bytes. A real nonblocking pipe accepts a prefix then reports a partial multi-argument write count between 512 and 2^17 while the same implementation's child receives exactly 10000 bytes. Close waits for receiver completion. The Windows native equivalent preserves actual partial IO, ordering and cleanup.
A file of 5001*13+6 bytes reads identically as a whole, as differently sized segments including zero-length, and as a large line plus final text. EOF and cleanup are verified.

Invalid popen modes fail. Pipe write/read round-trips and temporary cleanup work. Every shell command's popen-close status matches execute: success, missing command, exit 3/129, direct HUP/KILL signals, nested-shell termination, an empty same-executable command and typed exits 0/20 with state closure. Windows mapping replaces native shell syntax/status assumptions, not Lua success/failure semantics.

io.tmpfile returns a real file, supports write/seek/read and remains eligible for close-time finalization. The enclosing temporary-path guard ends here; the following date tests also run when IO was skipped, so their output is not sufficient IO evidence.

Date formatting preserves empty strings, embedded NUL and long literal/repeated conversion strings. Current and selected epoch boundary timestamps round-trip through date tables. Dynamically generated Lua assertions compare all calendar fields, weekday and yearday against formatting and are actually loaded/executed.

Unsupported or incomplete conversions fail, noninteger and missing time fields produce the expected diagnostics, and native-int year limits are checked without arithmetic overflow under the actual integer-width guards.

sections.guard: _port unset plus actual native int/time widths
sections.invariant: POSIX E/O modifiers, signed 31-bit second normalization and native representability limits are exercised. Dynamic time_t probing selects the original branch; every rejected day/month/year bound and final-second overflow retains its specific failure. Windows uses the source-hashed CRT-compatible date/range counterparts. macOS must use observed native behavior.

Date tables expose boolean DST where available and reconstruct current time with default DST inference. difftime handles leap-year intervals and signed differences. Negative seconds normalize all date-table fields across the year boundary, including yearday 366.

Default output is restored to stdout, parsed current calendar fields produce the final date/time line, and the exact Lua version line terminates output. Acceptance checks this witness together with every IO guard, expected stderr, subprocess configuration and balanced physical shutdown.
